page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-32 is a compute-focused instance within the N2D family, configured with 32 vCPUs and 32 GB of system RAM. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor built on x86_64 architecture, the machine provisions 16 physical cores across 32 threads. Cache hierarchy comprises 32 KB L1 data cache, 0.5 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB of shared L3 cache. Instruction set flags include AVX, AES, VAES, SHA-NI, BMI2, ADX, and FMA, although AVX-512 and AMX extensions are absent. The configuration does not include local storage or discrete GPU accelerators, relying on network-attached persistent storage.

Benchmark data displays solid baseline performance, highlighted by a strong top-25% result in stress-ng single-core execution (2692.17) alongside an average multi-core score of 43102.09. General computational suites reflect mid-tier throughput, recording a Geekbench single-core score of 1515.0 and multi-core score of 13313.0, with PassMark measuring a total CPU score of 39021.26. Memory subsystem performance shows 117.34 GB/sec read and 63.89 GB/sec write throughput on large 256MB blocks. In edge inference evaluating small 135M language models, text generation speed reached a strong 298.13 tokens per second.

Operating with a strict 1:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio of 1.0 GB per vCPU, the instance prioritizes raw processor parallelization over extensive in-memory capacities. This provides cost efficiency for multi-threaded computations that do not incur high per-core RAM footprints, avoiding payment for idle memory allocations. Conversely, the absence of high-density RAM and local NVMe storage limits its utility for large enterprise databases or massive dataset caches.

Workloads best aligned with the n2d-highcpu-32 include distributed build and compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch processing, image and video manipulation, and lightweight multi-threaded services that scale linearly across 32 dedicated threads.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2d-highcpu-32 is an x86_64 compute-oriented virtual machine featuring 32 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM, backed by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor with 16 physical cores and 32 threads. Offering a lean 1:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio, the instance is engineered for workloads requiring high thread density without overhead costs for unused memory. The system contains no integrated GPUs or local NVMe storage, utilizing remote block storage for persistence. In benchmarks, the instance demonstrates strong single-core performance alongside consistent mid-tier multi-core, cryptographic, and memory metrics, including 117.34 GB/sec read bandwidth on large memory blocks. It is well matched for software compilation, batch processing, media encoding, and compute-heavy containerized services.
